2609.30167.title: Do Audio Language Models Hear and Read Distinctive Features Alike?
2609.30167.paper_summary: Audio language models pass speech and text through a single decoder. We ask whether that decoder represents a distinctive feature in the same direction when a phoneme is heard and when it is read. For minimal pairs of phonemes differing in one feature, we take the offset between the two members' mean representations. Averaging those offsets gives a direction for each stream, and we measure the cosine between the two. Because the two streams already agree about arbitrary phoneme pairs, we compare every measure against a reference built from random pairings rather than against zero. We apply this to 6 models, 7 features and 15 languages from 11 families. Only voicing in the two Qwen2.5-Omni models exceeds that reference after correction for multiple testing, and the reference varies by a factor of seven between models. In three of the six models, voicing has one direction in audio across the 14 languages with enough minimal pairs to measure it, and every language pair agrees in two of them. The model family, not the model size, predicts which stream represents a feature.
2609.30167.paper_summary_zh: 音頻語言模型通過單一解碼器處理語音和文本。我們詢問當聽到音素和閱讀音素時，該解碼器是否在相同方向上代表一個獨特的特徵。對於在一個特徵上有所不同的最小對音素，我們取兩個成員的平均表示之間的偏移量。對這些偏移量進行平均為每個流提供了一個方向，我們測量兩者之間的餘弦。由於這兩個流已經對任意音素對達成一致，我們將每個測量與從隨機配對構建的參考進行比較，而不是與零進行比較。我們將此應用於來自11個語言家族的6個模型、7個特徵和15種語言。只有在經過多重測試校正後，兩個Qwen2.5-Omni模型中的聲音特徵超過了該參考，並且該參考在模型之間的變化因子為七。在六個模型中的三個中，聲音特徵在14種具有足夠最小對的語言中在音頻中具有一個方向，並且每對語言在其中兩個中達成一致。模型家族，而不是模型大小，預測哪個流代表一個特徵。
2609.30167.author: Yuanhao Chen et.al.
